messages:
Alex: Heads-up — us-west1 spot GPUs started evicting about 40% of capacity a few minutes ago. A bunch of model-serving pods restarted. We don't have a single short checklist for interruption handling; can we draft one here so oncall can run it quickly?

Priya: Can you paste the eviction alert/logs? need to triage whether it's provider mass-evict or an internal autoscaler flapping.

ops-bot: [ALERT] spot-eviction event detected
node-group: wg-spot-usw1
evicted: 18
reason: scheduled-maintenance
window_start: 2026-02-15T18:32:00Z

Alex: Logs: `kubelet: eviction signal: PreemptibleInstanceTermination` and GCE metadata shows maintenance. Most pods are Restarting rather than Terminating.

Marco: Quick checklist suggestion (short, step-by-step):
1) Confirm event source (cloud provider vs internal) — check provider status & ops-bot.
2) Increase replicas on dedicated pool for critical services (if available).
3) Mark affected nodes unschedulable: `kubectl cordon <node>` and `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`.
4) Trigger fallback routing: update routing policy to prefer `dedicated` region/pool for low-latency keys.
5) If >10% capacity lost for >5min, page eng-oncall (pager duty) and eng-infra lead.

Priya: Additions: annotate pods with `serving.priority=critical|best-effort` so drain logic can evict best-effort first. Also add a short `kubectl` snippet to force-migrate long-running training jobs to spot-tolerant queue.

Sam: For model-serving specifically: enable prefix/KV cache warmup on dedicated instances before routing traffic (reduces QoS blips). Also consider transiently lowering batch size to keep latency SLOs while we scale.

Jen: Escalation path proposal (one-liner):
- Tier 1: oncall (eng-oncall) — try automated fallback and cordon/drain -> 0-10 min
- Tier 2: eng-infra lead + eng-runtime -> 10-30 min if impact >10% or critical jobs failing
- Tier 3: Ops exec + Sales SE notified -> 30+ min for customer-impacting incidents
Include Slack channel #incidents for cross-team comms.

Marco: Example fallback routing config snippet we use (conceptual):
```yaml
routing:
  - match: model:low_latency
    primary: dedicated-usw1
    fallback: spot-usw1
    fallback_threshold: 15% # percent loss before switching traffic
```

Alex: Good. Also add a quick `kubectl` one-liner to requeue best-effort pods: `kubectl get pods -l queue=spot -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl delete` (our controllers will recreate them on a tolerant queue).

Priya: I'll turn these into a short runbook section: "Spot/Preemptible Interruption — Quick Actions" and attach to the eng-infra runbooks. Alex — can you own the first draft? I'll review and add the paging thresholds.

Alex: Yep, I’ll draft it now and push to the runbook. Summary for the runbook: cause-check, cordon/drain, fallback routing, scale dedicated, annotate priorities, paging thresholds, cache warmup, tips for long-running jobs. Adding links to provider maintenance page and ops-bot playbook. :thumbsup:

Jen: Also add cost note: if we fallback to dedicated for >2 hours, finance alert to evaluate burn/commit tradeoffs.

Priya: Thanks — closing here. I'll watch for the runbook PR and link it in #incidents once merged. :eyes:
